news.title: Asamoah Gyan: 2010 Fifa World Cup penalty miss was a blessing in disguise
news.lede: Retired Ghana football national team captain Asamoah Gyan addresses the media at Nyayo National Stadium on August 2, 2026. Asamoah Gyan now spots a small pot belly. It is most noticeable when he slips into one of his sharp suits, where the tailored drape is forced to negotiate a slight midsection. Yet, the drip remains unmistakably fashionable.

news.title: EXPLAINER: World football split over Infantino future
news.lede: FIFA's bid to move past the biggest internal crisis of Gianni Infantino's reign is unlikely to end scrutiny of how world soccer is governed as questions linger on whether promised reforms will lead to meaningful change before the 2027 presidential election. A day after FIFA's leadership gathered in Rabat to publicly reaffirm support for Infantino, the governing body apologised to its 211 members for mistakes surrounding the abandoned proposal to sell a slice of the World Cup's commercial future. FIFA also pledged to review the processes that led to the controversy that sparked the fiercest revolt of Infantino's tenure after national federations complained they had been sidelined.

news.title: World Cup inspired fixture considered to shake-up grand final weekend
news.lede: The league could be set to see the grand final weekend turn into a festival of football with three additional matches in frame to take place before the decider. Nine’s Danny Weidler reports the NRL are considering adding a third-place play-off, an under-21s game and an All-Stars game to take place over the three days leading into the premiership match on Sunday, October 4. The Broncos are the reigning premiers of the NRL Getty. Bulldogs boss Aaron Warburton flagged the idea in the NRL’s chief executive meeting this week, drawing inspiration from the FIFA World Cup last month.

The quadrennial World Cup is a state-of-the-art competition.

news.title: Will Asia turn its back on Fifa chief Infantino amid global divide in football?
news.lede: As the fight for the heart and soul of world football rumbles into a second weekend, a much clearer picture of the battle lines has started to emerge and in some cases divisions within camps are already obvious. Firmly in the anti-Gianni Infantino brigade stands Uefa, and, as of Friday, on the other side of the field the football authorities of Africa and South America. In a statement that came as little surprise, Norway’s federation said the trust was gone and asked the Fifa president to resign. The head of the country’s governing body, Lise Klaveness, is among those many would back to take the under-fire Infantino’s place.

news.title: New claims against Infantino deepen a turbulent period for world football's governing body
news.lede: According to The Telegraph, the Italian-Swiss lawyer, who served as secretary general of European football's governing body from 2009 to 2016, also previously used his influence to secure a promotion for the same UEFA employee with whom he was in an intimate relationship. Infantino has categorically denied the allegations, according to the article, which was published on Saturday. When contacted by the Agence France-Presse (AFP) news agency on Saturday, a FIFA spokesperson had not responded. According to The Telegraph, which did not cite its sources, this employee received a "six-figure sum" upon her departure — at an unspecified time — in addition to the payment of tuition fees for a business school amounting to around £45,000 (AU$86,000).

news.title: ‘Will not tolerate’: FIFA dig heels in as feisty statement fires back at president’s enemies
news.lede: FIFA have condemned efforts to oust Gianni Infantino as the governing body’s president in a statement released in response to allegations of an affair with a colleague during Infantino’s time as UEFA’s secretary-general. A FIFA spokesperson told the Telegraph, who originally reported the details of the alleged affair, promotion to a managerial role, six-figure sum payout upon departure and payment for business school, that Infantino “strongly denies” the allegations and that they are “categorically untrue”. news.title: "There Was a Reason for 'Messi's Tears' at the World Cup": Father Jorge Passes Away at 68; "The Quiet Supporter Who Created the 'God of Football'"
news.lede: 'God of Football' Lionel Messi (39, Inter Miami)'s father and long-time supporter, Jorge Messi, has passed away at the age of 68. According to Argentine media outlets Clarin and Infobae on the 8th (local time), Jorge Messi died in a hospital in Rosario, Argentina, after battling a chronic illness for a long time. He was more than just a father; he was the person who raised Messi into the world's best soccer player. In 2000, at age 13 when Messi required growth hormone treatment, Jorge traveled directly to Spain to secure Messi's signing and support contract with FC Barcelona.
